conviction_note: The guide is company arithmetic: FY26 adj. EBITDA +45-55% on $310M is $450-481M; less H1's $295M that leaves only $155-186M for H2 (about $78-93M a quarter) against Q2's $139M ex-lag. Against that, the Q3 metal price lag turns unfavourable (Midwest transaction price down about 8% Q2 to Q3) and metal fell again into October. The bar is one stale estimate that disagrees with itself ($2.00 vs $2.37), so the positive finding is capped and p_up is only 58. The findings sum to +0.8 and the scaled number is +1.44 on a 9% expected absolute move; the two measurements agree in sign.
bar: Q3 2026 adj. EPS: one analyst estimate. MarketBeat's page shows $2.00 in its estimates table and $2.37 in its earnings-history table (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/KALU/earnings/, read 2026-10-21), so the bar is disputed and every finding is capped. Company guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/811596/000119312526312472/kalu-ex99_1.htm, 2026-07-22): FY26 conversion revenue at the high end of +10-15%; adj. EBITDA +45-55% YoY on FY25's $310M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/811596/000119312526057221/kalu-ex99_1.htm); neutral metal lag assumed for the rest of the year. That implies $78-93M of adj. EBITDA a quarter in H2. My estimate of about $2.8-3.3 adj. EPS (EBITDA about $105-120M after roughly $20M of unfavourable lag) is +30% against a ~$2.2 midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest about 735K shares, ~4.5% of float, ~2.6 days to cover (Equibles snapshot ~2026-08-19, https://equibles.com/stocks/KALU, via the sweep row). Benzinga showed 7.0% short float in late September (via the sweep row; not re-verified because the search budget was exhausted). Not a crowded short. Tape: spot 152.45, 22% below the 2026-08-12 intraday high of 199.89. The stock fell 13.1% on 2026-08-18, the day after the CEO-succession release. 20-day run-up -2.4%, 5-day +2.9%.

findings.finding: The FY26 guide leaves only $155-186M of adj. EBITDA for H2 (about $78-93M a quarter), because FY26 is guided at +45-55% on FY25's $310M (= $450-481M) and H1 already delivered $295M ($129M + $166M). Q2's underlying, ex-lag EBITDA was $139M ($166M less $27M of lag). Q3 is seasonally no weaker on an ex-lag basis: Q3 2025 was about $53M against Q2 2025's $54M, derived from FY25 $310M, Q4 $88M with $29M lag and H1 lag $36M. The lone Q3 EPS estimate ($2.00-2.37) maps to about $85-95M of EBITDA, so a fourth straight large beat and a further FY raise are likely unless underlying margin collapses. The prior beats were Q1 $3.74 vs $1.96 and Q2 $5.53 vs $2.66.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Big beats with raises bought on day 1: Q2 2026 (EPS $5.53 vs $2.66, EBITDA guide raised from +20-30% to +45-55%) +9.91%, but it gave back 9.65% the next session. Q1 2026 (EPS $3.74 vs $1.96, guide raised) +1.11%. Q3 2025 (EPS $1.86 vs $0.80) +19.54%. Q4 2025 (in line, $1.53 vs $1.56) -8.85%.
findings.why_not_priced: The only published estimate ($2.00, or $2.37 on another table of the same page) is the guide's arithmetic and has trailed actuals by roughly $1.8-2.9 for two quarters. If the street had priced the run-rate, the estimate would sit above $3 and the stock would not be 22% off its August high, with the H2 guide unrevised since July. The caveat is that the company said it does not assume a continuation of the 'consumption cost tailwinds'. Part of Q2's $139M underlying may be temporary, which is why this is sized at the cap rather than on the name's 7.4% median.
findings.independence: FY25 base and lag figures come from the Q4 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/811596/000119312526057221/kalu-ex99_1.htm) and the Q1 figures from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/811596/000119312526170615/kalu-ex99_1.htm, which are the same company's documents and not independent. Consensus history: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/KALU/earnings/. This is the ex-lag view; the lag is filed separately below so the fact is not counted twice.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 metal price lag likely turns unfavourable after +$36M (Q1) and +$27M (Q2). LME aluminium cash averaged about $3,577/t in Q2 (Apr 3,601, May 3,670, Jun 3,459) and about $3,228/t in Q3 (Jul 3,156, Aug 3,250, Sep 3,277), down roughly 10%. The CME Midwest premium (AUP) fell from about $1.15-1.17/lb in Q2 to $1.07-1.12 in Q3. So the Midwest transaction price fell about 8% (about 22c/lb), most of it in the last week of June. On Kaiser's 2025-26 lag sensitivity (about $100M of lag per $1/lb move), that is roughly -$15M to -$25M against a guide that assumes a neutral lag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There has been no unfavourable-lag quarter in the 8-print history: lag was favourable through 2025 ($93M) and H1 2026 ($64M). Q4 2025, the one quarter where the beat was absent, fell 8.85%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the June drop came before the July 22 guide, and metal-literate holders track MWTP. But the lone estimate is built on the company's neutral-lag convention, so a negative lag line is not in the bar. If it were priced, the estimate would be below the guide pace, not at it.
findings.independence: The CME Midwest premium series is at https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/AUP=F?range=9mo&interval=1wk (weekly closes, Q2 about 1.15, Q3 about 1.09). Alcoa's Q3 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1675149/000119312526422891/aa-ex99_1.htm, 2026-10-15) shows its average realised third-party aluminium price at $4,527/t in Q3 against $4,752 in Q2 (-4.7%). That is a global realised price, so it is a proxy.

findings.finding: Metal is still falling into the Q4 outlook. LME cash averaged $3,059/t over Oct 1-20 against $3,277 in September (-6.7%) and printed $3,003.50 on 2026-10-20, its lowest since early January 2026. AUP's weekly close was $1.069/lb in the week of 10-19, against about $1.09 in mid-September, and a $1.00 intraday print on 2026-10-21 that may be a roll artefact. A Q4 that re-marks lag to current futures would temper the size of any FY raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance direction set the sign in each of the last four prints: two raises rose (+9.91% and +1.11%), the flat Q4 2025 fell 8.85%.
findings.why_not_priced: The October metal decline is public, but the company's outlook convention ('neutral metal lag') means the lone estimate ignores it. If the street had priced it, the FY estimate would sit below the guide high end rather than on the guide.
findings.independence: Same Westmetall document as the Q3 lag finding, different months, so not fully independent. AUP is at https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/AUP=F?range=9mo&interval=1wk. Alcoa guided Q4 Aluminum segment EBITDA about $30M lower sequentially on raw materials and maintenance (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1675149/000119312526422891/aa-ex99_1.htm), which is a different mechanism.

findings.finding: The CEO handover is inside the window. The 2026-10-22 call is Keith Harvey's last as CEO before Fred Stephan (ex-COO of Amcor Global Flexible Packaging) takes over on 2026-11-01; Harvey becomes Executive Chairman and advisor through 2027-10-31. The stock fell 13.1% on 2026-08-18, the session after the announcement, on 477K shares (2.7x its 20-day average) and has not recovered. The call is the first public chance to address continuity of strategy and capital allocation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior CEO transition in the baseline. The announcement itself cost 13.1% in one session (185.50 to 161.24).
findings.why_not_priced: The de-rating happened, so the risk is in the price. Any reassurance on the call (continuity, Harvey staying engaged, a packaging-heavy strategy Stephan knows) is an upside option the price does not carry. If the market had already been reassured, the stock would have retraced the August 18 gap.
findings.independence: The price reaction is from https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/KALU?range=6mo&interval=1d (the tape), which is different from the release. Nothing else.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew to cut against. A long lean on a name 22% below its August high, with a -2.4% 20-day run-up, works against the drawdown, but the drawdown has a dated cause (the CEO-succession gap of 08-18 plus falling metal) rather than a fundamental warning. The lean is therefore taken at only 58.
lessons_applied: Lesson 8 (thin coverage, a company-arithmetic number): abs_move_pct raised from 8.5 to 9.0. The guidance finding stays capped at +2.5 under lesson 6 because the lone bar is disputed ($2.00 vs $2.37).

Lesson 3 / two readings of one document: the guide-arithmetic finding was reframed as ex-lag so it does not also carry the Q3 lag, which is its own finding. Sizes unchanged, and independence now states the shared documents.
Lesson 7: short interest checked before the two negatives (4.5-7% of float, 2.6 days to cover, not crowded), so neither negative was shrunk.
Findings were reordered (guidance first); the sum is unchanged at +0.8.
